changelog.change: Initial entry — an interactive companion to peds-cardiac-arrest and pedi-tape-weight-zones: enter one weight (or an age estimate) and every weight-based resus number is pre-computed for the pre-arrival window. Equipment sizing and age-based rules (ETT, SBP floor) stay in the body.

purpose: Enter the child's weight ONCE, before they arrive, and read every weight-based resuscitation number pre-computed — so there is no arithmetic during the resuscitation. Doses are live from the exact weight; the caps and the equipment/age rules are below.

interpretation.label: Single-dose ceilings: epinephrine 1 mg, atropine 0.5 mg (child) / 1 mg (adolescent), adenosine 6 then 12 mg, amiodarone 300 mg, magnesium 2 g, naloxone 2 mg. Epinephrine repeats q3-5 min in arrest.

Cap subsequent defibrillation at 10 J/kg or the adult dose, whichever is lower. Cardioversion: PALS first-attempt range is 0.5-1 J/kg — the figure shown is the 1 J/kg end; drop to 0.5 J/kg for a first attempt in a stable-ish rhythm, then double.

embeddedCalculator.notes: This is the weight-derived arithmetic only. It is not a resuscitation algorithm — see `peds-cardiac-arrest` for the scenario cards (bradycardia, SVT, shockable/non-shockable arrest, torsades, hyperkalaemia) and the CPR mechanics, and the individual resus drug cards for infusions and full detail. Weigh the child if at all possible; use an age estimate only when a weight is genuinely unmeasurable.
embeddedCalculator.buildNote: Formula engine, min()/max() caps. Holliday-Segar rate is expressed with piecewise min/max since the engine has no conditional. Cardioversion 1st-dose shown at the 1 J/kg end of the PALS 0.5-1 range (stated in interpretation).

body.text: Age → weight estimate (only if a weight is unmeasurable)
An age-estimated weight must be treated as approximate — re-dose off a measured weight as soon as one is available, and flag the estimate to the team.
Age-based rules the weight can't give you

items: ETT size: uncuffed = (age/4) + 4; cuffed = (age/4) + 3.5. Depth at lip ≈ ETT size × 3, or (age/2) + 12. Cuffed tubes are preferred beyond the neonatal period (cuff pressure < 20-25 cmH2O).
Lowest acceptable systolic BP ≈ 70 + (2 × age in years) for ages 1-10; < 70 mmHg is hypotension in a neonate or infant.
Defibrillation pad size / placement and the ped-to-adult crossover depend on the specific device — verify against the unit in use (the Rust zone is the nominal transition).

body.text: For the resuscitation itself — the scenario-by-scenario numbers and CPR mechanics — use `peds-cardiac-arrest`. For equipment detail and the age-estimate rationale, `pedi-tape-weight-zones`. This card exists to get the arithmetic done before the patient is in the room.
